pmid.notes: PubMed ID provided as paper_id input.

country.evidence_quote: Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine, 7 avenue des Hauts-Fourneaux, 4362 Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg
country.notes: Study location inferred from affiliations and cohort sourcing from Centre Hospitalier du Luxembourg.

body_site.evidence_quote: Faecal samples were self-collected at three time points

bmi.notes: BMI mentioned as measured parameter but values not reported in main text; data in Supplementary Table 1 not provided.

disease.evidence_quote: case study of familial type 1 diabetes. T1DM was in all cases diagnosed for more than five years
disease.section: Study cohort and microbial community structures
disease.notes: Study focused on type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) in families. Healthy family members also included as controls.

disease_details.notes: No specific disease subtypes, complications, or detailed phenotypic details reported.

feces_phenotype.notes: Faecal samples were collected but no stool phenotypes (e.g., consistency, color) reported.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: α-amylase proteins AMY2A and AMY2B, carboxypeptidase CPA1 and CUZD1 to be less abundant; lactotransferrin (LTF) and intelectin (ITLN1) with higher abundance
biomarker_name.section: Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions
biomarker_name.notes: These are the primary biomarkers identified as differentially abundant in individuals with T1DM compared to healthy relatives.

biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type (proteins measured as relative abundance %, transcripts as normalized reads).

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: four proteins preferentially expressed in exocrine pancreas to be less abundant in stool of individuals with T1DM; LTF and ITLN1 with higher abundance
biomarker_value.section: Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions
biomarker_value.notes: Specific quantitative values not provided; only directional changes reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Overall survival not measured in this study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not reported; this is a microbiome study, not an oncology trial.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Analysis of intra- and inter-individual variation demonstrates that family membership has a pronounced effect on the structural and functional composition of the gastrointestinal microbiome.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal samples analyzed at metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metaproteomic levels for microbial community characterization.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: No tumor measurements reported; not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: No tumor residual measurements; study focuses on microbiome composition in type 1 diabetes families.

value: Study cohort: 20 individuals from 4 families across at least 2 generations with ≥2 T1DM cases each
Sample collection: 53 faecal samples over 2-4 months
T1DM diagnosis: >5 years with successful insulin replacement therapy
Metagenomic data: 3.9 ± 0.1 Gbp per sample (mean ± SD)
Metaproteomic data: 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra per sample
Healthy family members used as stringent control group
No consistent taxonomic differences across families in T1DM
Family membership stratifies cohort more strongly than other factors
Individual microbiome signatures persist across all omic levels
